claim: On October 7, 1933, Prof. Albert Einstein sailed for New York from Southampton, England.

evidence.quote:
SOUTHAMPTON. England. October
7 (/?•).—Prof. Albert Einstein sailed for

evidence.locator: full_text, page 3, 'EINSTEIN SAILS FOR U. S.' (AP)

notes: Round 9 (globe-to-map, 2026-10-29): the departure leg of the 1933 crossing that ends in EIN-F-0122 (arrived New York on the Westernland, October 17, 1933). The AP text spells the liner 'Western Land'; the claim leaves the ship out (EIN-F-0122 carries it). Same text: his wife 'had embarked at Antwerp' (the liner's earlier port; not claimed for him). A Springfield weekly Republican item (1933-10-19, p. 14) says the Westernland called at Halifax, N. S., on October 15 on the way; not staged. Washington Journal (German-language) 1933-10-13 p. 8 says the same in German; not used (G2 is English-only).
